title: Introduce lightweight CI emulator and shared cache protocol to speed local dev feedback
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Adds a lightweight local CI emulator (ci-emu) and a small, versioned cache protocol for ephemeral runners to speed developer iteration. No runtime behavior changes to production workflows; opt-in for devs and repo maintainers.
description: Summary: This PR introduces a small cross-platform CI emulator (ci-emu) and a tiny shared cache protocol that together let engineers run a faithful, fast subset of our GitHub Actions pipelines locally or in ephemeral CI. Motivation: developers today wait multiple minutes for CI feedback from full workflows. The emulator reproduces job ordering, environment variable injection, matrix selection pruning, and artifact/cache lookup semantics but runs tasks locally (or in a remote dev runner) with a fraction of the overhead. The cache protocol is intentionally minimal (versioned headers + content-addressed blobs) to allow safe sharing between ephemeral runners and local dev without requiring a centralized service. Goals: 1) reduce round-trip time for lint/test/fast-integration by ~3-5x for most changes, 2) shrink the need to run full matrix jobs during early iteration, 3) keep production release pipelines untouched and gated. What changed (high level): - tools/ci/ci-emu/ : new Go-based emulator binary and small config loader (cli + library) - infra/ci/cache-protocol.md : spec for the cache protocol (HTTP headers, blob layout, simple attestation) - .github/workflows/ci-lite.yml : new lightweight workflow that calls the emulator in remote runner mode for ephemeral CI - scripts/ci/patch-workflow.sh : helper to run emulated subsets locally with the same env as Actions - ci/pinning/actions-versions.json : added pins for a couple of actions used by the emulator to reduce runtime surprises - docs/dev/ci-emulator.md : onboarding and troubleshooting guide Design notes: - ci-emu intentionally executes user-defined commands (make test, ./scripts/run-lint) in separate processes and captures stdout/stderr with timestamps so output ordering mirrors Actions logs. - The cache protocol uses a small JSON header with schema v1 and a content-addressed blob (sha256). Servers can implement it behind any transport; our implementation includes a tiny in-repo file-backed store for dev and a simple ephemeral s3-compatible example for CI. - Security: the emulator does not attempt to expose secrets; it only replays env vars provided by workflows. We added a whitelist for envs and a --allow-secrets flag for opt-in scenarios. - Non-goal: this change is not a full replacement for Actions; production release, E2E, and long-running matrix jobs still use the existing workflows. Commits summary: - Add ci-emu CLI + library (portions of the runtime runner moved from dev-scripts) - Add cache protocol spec and local file store implementation - Introduce ci-lite workflow and hook into dev docs - Add tests for emulator behavior and basic protocol conformance - Fix linting issues surfaced by running emulator pipelines Files changed (high level): - tools/ci/ci-emu/main.go (new) - tools/ci/ci-emu/runner/*.go (new) - infra/ci/cache-protocol.md (new) - .github/workflows/ci-lite.yml (new) - scripts/ci/patch-workflow.sh (new) - docs/dev/ci-emulator.md (new) - ci/pinning/actions-versions.json (modified) - scripts/ci/emulator-integration-test.sh (new) - workspace/config/dev-cache-store.go (new) - Makefile (changed) CI results and iteration: - Initial CI run: lint failed (golangci-lint rule for error wrapping). I pushed a follow-up fix in the same branch. - Unit/integration tests for ci-emu passed locally and in CI on the second run. - E2E matrix jobs were left unchanged and continued to pass in parallel. - Final CI status: all checks passed, coverage slightly increased for the runner package. Review conversation (condensed): - Ethan Liu: requested clearer separation between emulator env and production secrets; asked for a safe default to avoid accidental secret leakage. Response: added env whitelist + --allow-secrets opt-in and documented in dev guide. - Priya Kapoor: asked for a migration plan for maintainers to adopt the lightweight workflow. Response: added docs/dev/ci-emulator.md with suggested adoption steps and a checklist. - Marco Alvarez: requested tests for cache protocol version negotiation; added protocol unit tests and a test harness simulating two store backends. - Automation: added a small gating job that ensures ci-lite.yml does not run on release branches by mistake. Risk and rollout: - Opt-in for teams: new ci-lite workflow will not replace existing CI; maintainers can enable it by adding a small file in .github/ci-enabled/<team>. - The cache protocol is v1 and includes a schema version in headers to allow future incompatible changes. - No production behavior change expected; all release automation and deploy flows remain on the main workflows. Backwards compatibility: - No breaking changes to public APIs or release mechanics. - Developers can continue to run existing scripts; ci-emu is an additional option. Follow-ups and TODOs: - Evaluate telemetry for emulator adoption (ENG-1010) and add anonymous opt-in usage pings. - Add a minimal VS Code extension snippet to invoke ci-emu from the editor. - Explore using the cache protocol for model-metadata artifacts in Dedicated test harnesses. Merge and deployment: - Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-21 after approvals from the reviewer group. - Release note added to the changelog-dev internal doc. Links: linear tickets ENG-998, ENG-1010. Related PRs: refactor of dev-scripts (will follow in a separate PR).
notes: Opt-in developer feature; no changes to production release workflows.
